knowledge_gaps: Text fusion is a reasonable hypothesis, but the report does not explain how pooled title words will avoid reinforcing the broad lexical matches already identified as a failure. A scratch-trained encoder has no established understanding of compatibility, mood or purpose.

The experiment leaves tokenization, vocabulary construction scope, text length, encoder dimension, initialization scale, projection bias, regularization and missing-text handling unresolved. A gate initialized at 0.1 does not guarantee a small residual without controlling representation norms.

Baseline versus fusion measures the entire intervention. A parameter-matched ID-only control and a separately trained shuffled-text control would help distinguish useful text information from added capacity or regularization. These must remain separate single-model trials.

ModelView compatibility needs a concrete implementation: an effective item representation may not expose the embedding attributes expected by existing probes. Repeated token encoding for B×L training positions and full-catalog recommendations also requires bounded profiling, deduplication or chunking, and explicit cache invalidation.

The evaluation plan omits validation uncertainty and adaptive selection effects. Raw logit margins can increase through score scaling without improving ranking; they cannot establish better semantic discrimination. Sampled HR@10 and feedback from twenty training users do not establish full-catalog utility.

Originality 3 is plausible, but potential 7 and difficulty 4 are provisional. The references do not directly establish the effectiveness or engineering cost of scratch-trained pooled text fusion in GRU4Rec. A baseline-objective comparison may be a cheaper first experiment, depending on the supplied loss.
